Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a closed distal radius fracture of the wrist. Over six visits,
care consisted of immobilization, serial clinical examinations, and follow-up imaging. Radiographs and the physical examination
clearly confirm the fracture, and the described mechanism of injury is consistent with the findings. The patient reports no prior
injury to this wrist or the surrounding area, and no earlier treatment for the region is known. Management followed a typical
course: initial splinting, prgoression to a removable brace as healing advanced, and gradual reduction in visit frequency as
symptoms and range of motion improved. Billing records reflect single, non-duplicated charges for each service rendered. At last
follow-up the fracture shoewd expected healing, and the patient was released to graduated activity with home exercises and
return precautions reviewed.
